html:
A Lebanese singer, born Nouhad Haddad around 1934, who is one of the most loved voices in the Arab world and a symbol of Lebanon itself.

She began as a teenager in the chorus of Lebanese radio. There she met the composers Assi and Mansour Rahbani, the Rahbani brothers, and married Assi in 1955. Together they made a new kind of Lebanese song: short, modern, mixing Arab and Western music, and full of village life, love and longing. They also staged musical plays, and her appearances at the Baalbeck Festival from 1957 made her a star.

Her songs are played across the Arab world in the morning, on radio and in cafes and taxis. They include songs for Jerusalem and Mecca and for Beirut.

During the civil war of 1975 to 1990 she stayed in Beirut and refused to sing in a divided country. Her song "Li Beirut" became an anthem for the city. Later she worked with her son, the composer Ziad Rahbani, who brought jazz into her music.
